og.h1: Where your industry hires. Find your row.

slides.text: Almost nobody switches industry. People switch companies, cities and titles, and stay in the sector they already know. So the useful question isn't what's hiring in India. It's where your industry hires, and whether that's anywhere near you.

slides.kicker: Share of each industry's openings, by metro
slides.note: Read your row, not the column totals. The row is your career.

slides.text: Your city is already decided. Technology puts 58.8% of its openings in Bengaluru and 20.0% in Hyderabad. Four in five tech jobs sit in two cities. Mumbai holds 2.9% of them, which is 49 openings from the 60 tech employers on this list.

Stay where you are. Mumbai is banking's biggest metro and holds only 16.5%. 42.4% of BFSI openings sit outside the six big metros — 2,107 jobs, more than the entire national technology total of 1,701. Everyone assumes finance means Mumbai. Branches are in every district, and the hiring follows the branches.

One number reframes the table. Technology has 60 employers here, more than any other industry, and 1,701 jobs. Consulting has 24 employers and 5,785. More companies hiring in your sector does not mean more jobs in it.

slides.h1: Find your row. Then check your postcode.
slides.sub: If your city's share trails Bengaluru's by more than ten points, the city is costing you more than your CV is.
